To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

HTP methods can be successfully used in academic labs for solving challenging targets, and that the best HTP protocols for any given target class are the ones that were developed specifically for that class.
HTP is a great tool to solve structures, but it is not a silver bullet, it requires a lot of effort and expertise and it is not for everybody.

the combination of HTP and expertise is a powerful approach to solve the structures of challenging targets and that the best way to achieve this goal is by using the HTP approach as a screening method and not as a solution method.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development, optimization and validation of HTP methods for structural studies on challenging targets, and with their application to the elucidation of molecular mechanisms in biology and medicine.
developing, optimizing and implementing HTP technologies for structural and functional analysis of challenging biological systems.
the development of new methods to study the structural basis of biological function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HTP methods are not a panacea but can help to solve a lot of problems if used with care and with a clear understanding of the underlying biology and the target structure.
HTP methods are indispensable in the structural biology toolbox of any group aiming to solve a significant number of challenging targets.

, yes, HTP can be a very efficient and effective approach to structure solution, but only if the HTP platform is designed to fit the needs of the individual projects and targets, and not the other way around.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HTP is an indispensable technology for solving challenging targets, but it is not a substitute for the individual target expertise.
, with the right technology, the right expertise, and the right project management, HTP crystallography can be a very powerful and efficient tool to solve structures of difficult targets.
HTP is a powerful tool for the study of challenging targets, and that the technology can be adapted and implemented in a small group environment, even with limited resources.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the HTP approach is a very efficient way of solving structures of challenging proteins, provided that it is implemented with a clear understanding of the strengths and limitations of the methods and with a well defined strategy to address the challenges of the particular target class.

HTP screening methods are not only applicable to SG projects but also to individual projects, even when dealing with difficult targets, and that the combination of HTP screening methods with thorough characterization of the individual target can be a very powerful approach for structural and functional biology.

, despite the many pitfalls and challenges, the combination of high throughput screening methods and dedicated expertise can provide a powerful platform for solving the structures of challenging targets.
